points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (retaining its value/persisting across function calls), unlike a non-static array which is re-initialized each time the function is called.
points.partial_credit: Award 2-3 marks for a related but incomplete statement, e.g. static arrays keep their values/persist between calls or exist for the whole program, without mentioning one-time initialization or contrasting with non-static.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a static array is initialized only once (or keeps its values between function calls), in any wording, even briefly. Part marks for a vague or half-right statement such as static arrays persisting or having program-long lifetime without the initialization point. No marks for unrelated points (e.g. array size or syntax) that don't address the difference.
